  "body": "# FunC cookbook (https://docs.ton.org/llms/languages/func/cookbook/content.md)



<Callout type="note">
  The official smart contract language of TON Blockchain is [Tolk](https://docs.ton.org/llms/tolk/overview/content.md). FunC is now a **legacy** language, with its compiler no longer maintained.

  Learn how to [migrate from FunC to Tolk](https://docs.ton.org/llms/tolk/from-func/tolk-vs-func/content.md). For new smart contract projects, use the [Acton toolchain](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/acton/content.md).
</Callout>

The FunC cookbook was created to consolidate all the knowledge and best practices from experienced FunC developers in one place.
The goal is to make it easier for future developers to build smart contracts efficiently.

Unlike the rest of the official FunC documentation, this guide focuses on solving everyday challenges that FunC developers encounter
during smart contract development.

## Statements [#statements]

### How to use flags in if statements [#how-to-use-flags-in-if-statements]

To check whether an event is relevant, use a flag variable of type integer.
The flag can either be `0`, representing `false`, or `-1`, representing `true`.
See [absence of boolean type](https://docs.ton.org/llms/languages/func/types/content.md).

When checking the flag in [`if...else` statements](https://docs.ton.org/llms/languages/func/statements/content.md), it is unnecessary to use
the [`==` operator](https://docs.ton.org/llms/languages/func/operators/content.md), since a `0` evaluates to `false`, and any nonzero value is
considered to be `true` in `if..else` statements.

```func
int flag = 0;  ;; false

;; ...
;; ...

if (flag) {    ;; No need to use flag == -1
    ;; do something
}
else {
    ;; reject
}
```

### How to write a repeat loop [#how-to-write-a-repeat-loop]

A [repeat loop](https://docs.ton.org/llms/languages/func/statements/content.md) helps execute an action a fixed number of times. The example below computes
exponentiation of `number` to the exponent `exponent`, and illustrates it with specific values `number = 2` and `exponent = 5`:

```func
int number = 2;
int exponent = 5;

int result = 1;      ;; Will store the final result: number^exponent

repeat(exponent) {   ;; The repeat multiplies variable "number",

[Tolk](https://docs.ton.org/llms/tolk/overview/content.md) is the recommended language for TON smart contracts. [Acton ↗️](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/acton/content.md) is the recommended all-in-one toolchain for the entire contract development lifecycle, including building, testing, and deploying Tolk contracts.

<Callout type="note" title="External documentation">
  [Acton ↗️](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/acton/content.md) documentation is hosted and updated externally.
</Callout>

Add support for the Acton toolchain, Tolk language, and intermediate TON languages to a local editor:

* [JetBrains IDEs](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/ide/jetbrains/content.md) — plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, CLion, PyCharm, and other JetBrains IDEs

Follow the [quickstart page in the Acton documentation](https://ton-blockchain.github.io/acton/docs/quickstart).
